ms.report:
We have completed the second Milestone. Since the first milestone, we have converted our NPM package from javascript to typescript. We made a decision to leave some backend mechanisms like data persistence and session management to the users of this package because implementing those in the NPM package would significantly limit customization of the apps developed with this package. Now the NPM package provides functions and components for both the client and server side of NextJS projects. The server side provides functions to signup and login users with either email and passwords or cardano wallets. The functions validate the ownership of Cardano wallets by message signing and verifying the signed message. The package also provides functions to the user of the package for them to implement their logic more freely. 
The demo app that shows the signup and login functionality: https://boilerplate-e.vercel.app/
The NPM Package: https://github.com/littlefish-foundation/boilerplate-e/tree/milestone-2-update
The detailed document about the usage of the package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/littlefish-nft-auth-framework-beta
Brief outline of the security measures: https://hackmd.io/@emirolgun/SkiisFGmC

ms.report:
We have extended our tests to cover the demo app as well as the framework. 
We have completed the third milestone. In addition to the previous functionalities, now the package can work with both Preprod and Mainnet wallets. signup and login functions support NFT and Token authentication. The asset authentication uses Blockfrost API to verify ownership of the provided assets. We also have developed different functions like policyID verifier for developers using our package. These functions can allow developers to implement their logic more freely. Signup and Login functions now also support strict authentication. Strict authentication means allowing only wallets with certain NFT collections to successfully authenticate. The demo app does not impose this strict authentication mechanism for people to try it.
We were using next-auth beta for our demo app, and it created several problems with authentication with CIP-30 wallets. We have recreated the authentication system and the demo app is fully functional now. The app allows signing up with any assets and wallets. If you signup with asset, you will not be able to login with just wallet, you need the asset as well. The demo app now has two pages, ADA Handle page and HOSKY page. Only accounts with those assets can access these pages. If you need to check the functionality and don't possess these assets, please contact us with an asset you have and we will add those asset to our database for you to test.
The demo app relies on cookies, the previous version gave errors when cookies were blocked, the updated version gives the proper warning.
The demo app that shows the signup and login functionality: https://boilerplate-e.vercel.app/

ms.report:
After utilizing one of the NFTs to sign in, the user must delete their account from the “User” page to test other NFTs. Failure to do so will result in the system anticipating access from the previously used NFT, causing an error.
We have developed a metadata standard, the functions in the package to validate and use the metadata standard, and the demo app functionality for the sso function of the metadata and the package. While developing the metadata standard we consulted with various developers such as Andrew Westberg and the Gimbalabs community.
After extensive deliberation, we have reached a consensus to refrain from implementing minting authentication assets. Our rationale stems from the fact that the minting process should be exclusively managed by application administrators rather than being accessible to the general public. This decision is driven by the paramount importance of the PolicyID and Asset Names as the most critical security features of the authentication assets. Consequently, we have determined that the control over these policies must be meticulously stringent.
Here is the proof advice from Andrew Westberg: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1BuXW3JGsik4_gz8zCp2uVhRF8WG7_Vnk/view?usp=sharing

We have successfully completed the Open Source NFT and Wallet Authentication Framework for Cardano, meeting all milestone objectives and delivering a robust authentication solution for dApps. The framework provides seamless wallet-based and NFT-based authentication, advanced SSO metadata functionality, and developer-friendly integration tools. We still include the Proof of Concept video since it explains the package comprehensively. We improved the Project Close-out Report according to the reviewer feedback.
